questions.stem: Akbar ascended the Mughal throne at Kalanaur in:
questions.explanation: Akbar — crowned at Kalanaur (Gurdaspur, Punjab) on 14 February 1556 at age 13, days after Humayun's death in an accident at Purana Qila stairs. Bairam Khan as regent till 1560. Won the Second Battle of Panipat against Hemu (5 Nov 1556). Reigned 49 years — died 1605.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Akbar's LAND REVENUE system — based on measurement, classification, and 1/3 demand — is called:
questions.explanation: Zabti — also known as Dahsala (10-year average). Designed by Raja Todar Mal (1580). 10-year price averages determined the cash rate per bigha per crop. Land classified: polaj (cultivated annually), parauti, chachar, banjar. Revenue 1/3 of produce. Effective in northern India.
questions.subject: History

options.option_text: Bairam Khan (was regent, died before the Navaratnas era)

questions.explanation: Bairam Khan — Akbar's regent (1556-60) but was dismissed and killed in 1561, before the Navaratnas court. The Navaratnas (~1570s onwards): Abul Fazl (Akbarnama), Faizi (poet), Tansen (musician), Raja Birbal, Raja Todar Mal (revenue), Raja Man Singh (military), Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana (poet/general), Mullah Do Piyaza, Fakir Aziao-Din.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Akbar ABOLISHED JIZYA (tax on non-Muslims) in the year:
questions.explanation: Akbar abolished Jizya in 1564. (Also abolished pilgrimage tax in 1563.) Aurangzeb re-imposed Jizya in 1679. Akbar also launched Din-i-Ilahi syncretic movement (1582), Ibadat Khana religious discussions at Fatehpur Sikri (1575).
questions.subject: History

questions.explanation: Abul Fazl — court historian, wrote Akbarnama (narrative history of Akbar's reign) + Ain-i-Akbari (statistical/administrative gazetteer — 3rd volume of Akbarnama). Badauni wrote a critical alternative (Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh). Nizamuddin wrote Tabaqat-i-Akbari.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Akbar built FATEHPUR SIKRI in memory of:

options.option_text: Sufi saint Sheikh Salim Chishti's blessing (birth of his son Jahangir)

questions.explanation: Fatehpur Sikri — ~40 km west of Agra. Akbar built it 1571 to honour Sheikh Salim Chishti, whose blessings produced his son Salim (later Jahangir). Served as capital 1571-85 then abandoned (water scarcity). UNESCO WHS. Contains Buland Darwaza, Jama Masjid, Panch Mahal, Salim Chishti dargah.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The FAITH Akbar promoted, blending elements of multiple religions, was called:
questions.explanation: Din-i-Ilahi ('Divine Faith') — 1582, syncretic belief system drawing on Islam, Hinduism, Jainism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism. Never widespread — mostly confined to Akbar's inner circle (Birbal was a notable adherent). Tauhid-i-Ilahi (monotheism) is sometimes used interchangeably.
